guard: the hermes Python lifecycle hooks can resolve the control token a managed launch gives them, and say so out loud when they cannot
why: THIS CELL EXISTS BECAUSE THE DEFECT IT GUARDS SHIPPED ON THIS BRANCH AND NO TEST SAW IT. When the
control token moved out of the seat environment into the launch-material file, every TypeScript
consumer was updated and proved. These hooks are PYTHON, they read the environment variable
directly, and they return early and silently when it is missing. Result: a hermes seat that joins
the mesh, runs its sidecar and bridge normally, and never moves off its first presence value, with
no error anywhere. A reviewer found it by reading the Python.
M1 IS THE DEFECT ITSELF, restored exactly: delete the material lookup and leave the environment
read. It must redden H1, the managed-launch case, which is the only leg that exercises a token
that exists ONLY in the material file.
M2 IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS MORE, and it is why H3 is in the suite at all. Restoring the SILENT
return - no warning on stderr - leaves a hook that still relays nothing and still tells nobody.
A suite that only checked the happy path would go green against that, and the operator would be
back to a seat whose presence is frozen for no visible reason. Naming H3 here is what makes
'it fails loudly' a tested property rather than an intention in a commit message.
NO BUILD STEP IS PREPENDED, deliberately, and it is not an oversight. The suite drives
`plugin/cotal/hooks.py` through a real `python3` with PYTHONPATH pointed at the plugin source.
Python has no dist/, so the mutation is read by the interpreter directly and the staleness trap
that forces `pnpm build` on the TypeScript mutations cannot apply here.
NO `completionMarker` IS DECLARED: the suite counts failures and prints its banner either way, but
the graded evidence is the named assertion, and the marker adds nothing a fail-fast reading would
not already give. The seat-env-scope config records what happens when a success banner is declared
as a marker on a suite that cannot print it.

mutations.name: M1 the Python hooks read only the environment, as they did before the fix
mutations.expectRed: H1: a managed launch relays one frame with the token from the launch material
mutations.note: The shipped defect, restored. H2 (standalone, token exported directly) stays green under it, which is the point: the broken build looked healthy on every path anyone was testing.

mutations.name: M2 an unresolvable control token returns silently instead of warning
mutations.find:
_warn_once(
            "control socket is configured but no control token could be resolved "
mutations.replace:
_quiet_once(
            "control socket is configured but no control token could be resolved "
mutations.expectRed: H3: and it says so on stderr instead of returning silently (this is the whole defect)
mutations.note: A NameError inside a hook would be caught by the gateway rather than surfacing, so the mutant is a hook that produces nothing and says nothing - which is precisely the failure mode. H3 is the assertion that refuses to accept silence as success.
